title: Maintaining physical activity through digital tools for long-term conditions: A scoping review
author: Paul Clarkson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf7gjrjw
materials: Scoping studies: advancing the methodology Implementation Science

steps.title: Define Eligibility Criteria
steps.instruction: Establish inclusion and exclusion criteria for the scoping review.

substeps.instruction: Include all study types from 2009 - 2019.

Include long-term conditions: cardiovascular disease, myocardial infarction, stroke/TIA, Asthma, COPD, chronic kidney disease, diabetes mellitus, dementia, mental health, depression, osteoporosis, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, and obesity.
Include studies using terms 'long-term condition', 'chronic', or 'multimorbidity' if one or more of the specified conditions are present.
Exclude cancer and low back pain.
Include adults not maintaining 150 minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity per week.
Require follow-up of at least 3-months post-intervention.
Define digital tools according to World Health Organisation classification of digital health interventions v1.0.

steps.title: Execute Search Strategy
steps.instruction: Search relevant databases and registries for studies published between 2009 – 2019.

substeps.instruction: Consult with an academic librarian to establish a comprehensive list of search terms and strategy.
Search databases: CINAHL, Medline, OVID EMBASE, IEEE Xplore, PsycINFO, Scopus, and Google Scholar.
Search trial registries: PROSPERO, ISRCTN, ICTRP (WHO), EU clinical trials register, and Clinicaltrials.gov.
Search reference lists of eligible studies to identify additional missed studies.

steps.title: Select Sources of Evidence
steps.instruction: Screen titles, abstracts, and full texts to determine study eligibility.

substeps.instruction: Assess 5% of titles and abstracts using two independent reviewers to confirm eligibility criteria.
Divide title/abstract screening among the review team using Covidence software, with each item reviewed by two independent reviewers.
Resolve conflicts via an independent verifier.
Perform full-text screening using the same two-reviewer and verifier procedure.

steps.title: Chart Data
steps.instruction: Extract relevant data into a standardized format.

substeps.instruction: Chart data into a Microsoft Excel form based on review objectives.
Utilize an online portal for the charting form to allow team collaboration and discussion.

steps.title: Extract Specific Data Items
steps.instruction: Collect detailed information from the selected studies.

substeps.instruction: Extract data on digital tool type and contents, theoretical underpinning, user experience, and barriers/facilitators to use.
Extract effectiveness data to support potential future focused reviews.

steps.title: Synthesize Results
steps.instruction: Analyze and collate the extracted quantitative and qualitative data.

substeps.instruction: Collate and synthesize quantitative data descriptively.
Synthesize qualitative data using thematic analysis following the staged approach by Braun and Clarke.
Assign synthesis tasks to research team members based on their experience with quantitative and qualitative analysis.
